en.title: Snow forecast in Western Canada: up to 33 cm at Ski Callaghan by 6 November
en.description: Until 6 November, our forecast gives 33 cm at Ski Callaghan, 31 cm at Mount Cain Alpine Park and 25 cm at Whistler Blackcomb. Keep in mind: resort …
en.lede: Until 6 November, our forecast gives 33 cm at Ski Callaghan, 31 cm at Mount Cain Alpine Park and 25 cm at Whistler Blackcomb. Keep in mind: resort values come from our snow model and describe an area, while stations measure one point.

p: Until 6 November, our forecast gives 18 cm at Tweedsmuir Ski Club and 14 cm at Sasquatch.
The snow cover shrank from 370,180 km² on 1 November to 329,280 km² today, and our forecast gives 302,380 km² on 6 November.
At Ski Callaghan, the freezing level reaches 1,260 m to 2,050 m on 3 November, above the top of the resort (998 m): rain or wet snow is possible on every slope that day.
At Mount Cain Alpine Park, the freezing level reaches 2,060 m to 2,270 m on 3 November, above the top of the resort (1,616 m): rain or wet snow is possible on every slope that day.
At Whistler Blackcomb, the freezing level reaches 1,680 m to 2,240 m on 3 November, so the lower slopes may get wet snow while the top stays wintry.
Of these resorts, Mount Cain Alpine Park has the most snow on its upper slopes today, about 68 cm; then come Whistler Blackcomb 61 cm and Tweedsmuir Ski Club 21 cm.
Our snow model shows 329,280 km² of snow-covered ground in Western Canada today, with snow at 51 of 57 resorts.
Forecasts a few days ahead can change: look at the map again the day before you travel.

advice: Forecasts a few days ahead can change: look at the map again the day before you travel.
Where the freezing level goes above the resort, plan for wet snow and use the highest lifts.
Fresh snow is best in the first hours after it stops: go early, before the sun and the crowds.
Before you ski off-piste or go touring, read the official avalanche bulletin (links below).
Get a powder alert in the SnowScope app to know when Ski Callaghan gets fresh snow.
